# Incident Report: Koi Stealer Compromise — DESKTOP-RNVO9AT

**Evidence reviewed:** `2024-09-04-traffic-analysis-exercise.pcap` (5,091 frames), Suricata/Sguil alert export (`.txt` and `.jpg`)
**Analysis method:** tshark protocol/field extraction, TCP stream reassembly, HTTP object carving. No external lookups performed.

---

## 1. Infected Host

| Attribute | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| IPv4 address | **172.17.0.99** | Consistent across DHCP, ARP, NBNS, HTTP, Kerberos |
| MAC address | **18:3d:a2:b6:8d:c4** | DHCP Discover, ARP replies |
| Windows hostname | **DESKTOP-RNVO9AT** | DHCP Option 12 (hostname), NBNS name registration (`<00>`/`<20>`), DNS PTR queries for `DESKTOP-RNVO9AT.bepositive.com` |
| AD domain | BEPOSITIVE (bepositive.com) | Kerberos realm field, LDAP/CLDAP SRV queries |
| Logged-in user | **afletcher** | Kerberos AS-REQ/TGS-REQ `CNameString` fields, both request (172.17.0.99→172.17.0.17) and reply legs |
| Domain controller | WIN-CTL9XBQ9Y19 — 172.17.0.17, MAC 00:23:ae:50:ba:fd | NBNS `<20>` Server service, DNS `_ldap._tcp` SRV lookups |

This is the only host on the /24 (172.17.0.0/24) generating malicious C2 traffic; all alerts sourced from it.

---

## 2. Malware Family

**Koi Stealer** (Win32/Koi Stealer).

**Attribution: signature-confirmed.** The IDS fired `ETPRO TROJAN Win32/Koi Stealer CnC Checkin (POST) M2` 48 times (Sguil priority-1/escalated, shown in red in the alert console) against `172.17.0.99 → 79.124.78.197:80`, directly matching the HTTP POST beacon traffic captured in the pcap.

This is corroborated behaviorally by the reassembled TCP streams:
- Repeated `POST /foots.php` with `Content-Type: application/octet-stream`, `Content-Encoding: binary`, and a spoofed legacy user-agent (`Mozilla/4.0 (compatible; MSIE 7.0; ... Trident/7.0 ...)`), while the real host is Windows 10/11 with a modern default browser — a classic stealer/loader UA-spoofing pattern.
- Plaintext-visible message framing inside the encrypted-looking body: numeric command codes followed by a pipe-delimited bot GUID, e.g. `101|30168213-3be0-a751-81a0-cf3b228c8654|5LHtVruc|...`, `111|30168213-...|XHfhyxOtsArXQLiP|...`, `102|30168213-...` — consistent with a stealer check-in/exfil protocol.
- A companion gate/loader exchange on `/index.php` returning the plaintext token `HckDcK0czXjaq48jVHNn|qIOuKk7U|http://79.124.78.197/index.php|`, followed by an encrypted POST — typical pay-per-install "gate" behavior feeding the stealer.

---

## 3. Indicators of Compromise

### Command-and-control endpoint
- **79.124.78.197:80/tcp (HTTP)** — primary Koi Stealer C2. Contacted directly by hardcoded IP; no DNS query for this host was ever issued, consistent with a hardcoded C2 address.
  - Beacon window observed: **2024-09-04 17:35:07 UTC → 18:31:53 UTC** (48 checkins, ~1–2 min interval)
  - Bot ID: `30168213-3be0-a751-81a0-cf3b228c8654`
  - Affiliate/sub-ID: `qIOuKk7U`
  - Gate token: `HckDcK0czXjaq48jVHNn`

### Malicious URLs
- `http://79.124.78.197/foots.php` (POST, repeated — main C2 beacon/exfil channel)
- `http://79.124.78.197/index.php?id=&subid=qIOuKk7U` (GET — gate check-in)
- `http://79.124.78.197/index.php` (POST — encrypted payload/config exchange)

### Secondary suspicious indicator (behavioral, not signature-confirmed)
- **46.254.34.201:443/tcp**, TLS ClientHello SNI = `www.bellantonicioccolato.it` at 17:35:04 UTC — three seconds before the first Koi Stealer beacon. No DNS query for this domain appears anywhere in the capture, meaning the host connected to the IP directly and presented an unrelated legitimate-looking SNI. This pattern (hardcoded-IP connection + mismatched/benign SNI, no prior resolution) is consistent with SNI cloaking used to blend malicious TLS traffic into normal-looking logs. Traffic is TLS 1.3, so payload/certificate content could not be inspected; listed as a candidate pre-beacon C2/loader contact, not confirmed malicious.

### Transferred files / hashes
No plaintext executable (PE) payload was observed anywhere in the capture — carved HTTP objects on the C2 channel are opaque encrypted/binary blobs (`index.php` response, 105 bytes; POST body to `/index.php`, 105 bytes) with no recoverable filename or file signature (no `MZ` header found in any TCP payload). **No SHA256 hash can be derived from this evidence** — the infection vector/dropper is not present in this capture; only the post-infection C2 channel is visible.

### Alerts assessed as likely benign (not counted as IOCs)
- `ET INFO Terse Request for .txt - Likely Hostile` / `ET INFO Microsoft Connection Test` — legitimate Windows NCSI check to `www.msftconnecttest.com` (23.220.251.149/158).
- `GPL NETBIOS SMB ... NTMLSSP overflow`, `SMB IPC$ unicode share access`, `SMB_COM_TRANSACTION Max Data Count of 0 DOS Attempt`, `GPL RPC kerberos principal name overflow TCP` — all sourced `172.17.0.99 → 172.17.0.17:139/88`, coincident with normal domain-machine authentication (NTLMSSP session setup, Kerberos TGS/AS exchanges, DRSUAPI DsCrackNames and SAMR domain/user enumeration calls consistent with routine AD lookups, not DCSync — no `DRSGetNCChanges`/opnum 3 observed). These are generic/legacy GPL signatures known to fire on standard SMB/Kerberos byte patterns; no corroborating evidence of actual exploitation was found.
- `acroipm2.adobe.com GET /assets/Owner/arm/ProcessMAU.txt` — legitimate Adobe Update Manager telemetry check (4-byte placeholder response).
- All other DNS/TLS activity (msn.com, bing.com, Office/Microsoft telemetry, windowsupdate.com CRL fetches, login.microsoftonline.com) is standard Windows/Office background traffic.

---

## 4. Summary

`DESKTOP-RNVO9AT` (172.17.0.99, MAC 18:3d:a2:b6:8d:c4), logged in as domain user **afletcher** on the BEPOSITIVE.COM domain, is compromised with **Koi Stealer**, confirmed via signature match on its HTTP POST check-in traffic to **79.124.78.197:80**. The malware beaconed continuously for roughly one hour (17:35–18:32 UTC) using bot ID `30168213-3be0-a751-81a0-cf3b228c8654` and gate token `qIOuKk7U`/`HckDcK0czXjaq48jVHNn`. A likely pre-beacon contact to 46.254.34.201:443 with a spoofed/unresolved SNI should be treated as a related but unconfirmed indicator. No dropper file or hash is recoverable from this capture; recommend acquiring host-based forensics (disk/memory) from DESKTOP-RNVO9AT to identify the delivery mechanism and any dropped binaries, and block/monitor 79.124.78.197 and 46.254.34.201 network-wide.
